reader.decision: Approve the proposal with the read_at guard added to UPSERT_LATEST, as one change set. Keep the shorter-delays alternative as the fallback only if store.py cannot be changed today. Track the duplicate-row risk in readings as a separate follow-up item.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows that raising max_ack_pending to 256 lets an old retried reading overwrite a newer one in latest_reading, and the read_at guard closes that gap at the cost of one comparison per upsert. The guard also removes the blocking that kept lag up for 16 minutes after the failover. The duplicate-row risk is rare and applies to readings, not to the alert path, so it need not block approval.

reconstruction.problem: The hand-written retry loop in sparrow-ingest (with_retries, sleeping 2/4/8/16/32 s) runs with max_ack_pending: 1. It blocks every later reading for up to 62 s per failing message. During the 26 October failover, 17 stalls meant about 17.6 minutes of blocking, and lag took 16 minutes to clear.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Moving to JetStream redelivery with max_ack_pending 256 removes the accidental per-device ordering. UPSERT_LATEST has no read_at check, so a retried older reading (A) can overwrite a newer one (C) in latest_reading. The live map and the freezer-temp-high alert then read a stale value. The value stays stale until the next reading, or for good if A was the last reading before the device went offline. A second, rarer risk is that a lost ack after commit can insert a duplicate row in readings. readings has no visible unique key, so reports could double count.
reconstruction.fix: Delete ingest/retry.py. In ingest/handler.py, remove with_retries, call nak(delay=...) on TransientError, and publish to ingest.dlq and ack when num_delivered reaches 6. In deploy/consumer.yaml, set max_ack_pending to 256 and max_deliver to 6. In ingest/store.py, add WHERE latest_reading.read_at < EXCLUDED.read_at to UPSERT_LATEST so older readings do not overwrite newer ones.
reconstruction.cost: The guard costs one comparison per upsert. The retry schedule stays the same, with six attempts and the same delays. The remaining risk is rare duplicate rows in readings, which needs a separate item. The alternative of keeping max_ack_pending at 1 with shorter delays costs nothing in code but still blocks all readings during a failover.

follow_up_questions: Can store.py be changed and deployed today, so the guard ships together with the consumer change?
Is read_at set by the device or by the ingest service? The guard compares it, and the message does not say, so equal or skewed timestamps could be a problem.
reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve the proposal with the read_at guard added to UPSERT_LATEST. The guard must ship in the same change as the max_ack_pending increase. Raise the duplicate-row risk in readings as the next item.
